title: Which adjacent gate could explain two population measurements?
assumptions: The sites \(0,\ldots,N-1\) are arranged on a line, with \(N\ge2\). The input is a real unit vector \(x\). Two exact population reports \(p,q\) have nonnegative entries summing to one, with \(p_j=x_j^2\). The input signs are unreported.

The proposed explanation is exactly one operation on an edge \((i,i+1)\). On that ordered pair it applies \(R(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\ \sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}\) for an arbitrary real \(\theta\), fixing every other coordinate.
conventions: The angle may be zero. An explanation need only reproduce the output populations \(q_j\); no output signs are specified.
Write \(P_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k}p_j\) and \(Q_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k}q_j\) for the mass to the left of the cut between \(k\) and \(k+1\), where \(0\le k<N-1\).
question:
Using the two lists of cut masses, find every edge on which one gate could have produced the second report. Give a necessary and sufficient test and justify it for every choice of signs consistent with \(p\), allowing the angle to depend on the actual input. Explain what the test says when the reports agree and when the input has zero mass on the proposed pair.

For \(N=4\), suppose \(p=(1,2,1,4)/8\). Diagnose each proposed output \(q^{(1)}=(1,1,2,4)/8\) and \(q^{(2)}=(2,2,1,3)/8\). For each, give all possible edge locations or explain why no single gate fits.

declaration_spans.scope: Defines the signed half-angle update of the two selected real rows, leaving other rows unchanged. A single column gives the site-amplitude rule. The definition gives no test from probabilities, propagation bound or scheduling optimum.
For any two signed real numbers, the cosine and sine of half the split angle, multiplied by their Euclidean pair norm, reproduce the two numbers. This is a two-coordinate existence ingredient.
A basis column whose index is outside the two selected indices equals the corresponding identity column in every row.
The square of the real pair norm is the sum of the two squared entries. No graph or measurement identification is part of this equality.

reference_answer:
Let \(D_k=Q_k-P_k\) and put \(D_{-1}=D_{N-1}=0\), where the last equality follows from normalization. The set of compatible edge indices is \(\{i:0\le i<N-1,\ D_k=0\text{ for every }k\ne i,\ 0\le k<N-1\}\). Indeed, a gate on \((i,i+1)\) fixes every other amplitude and preserves \(x_i^2+x_{i+1}^2\). A prefix ending before \(i\) excludes both sites. A prefix ending after \(i\) includes both. Only the cut at \(i\) can change.

Conversely, if all differences away from cut \(i\) vanish, \(q_j-p_j=D_j-D_{j-1}\) shows that every outside population agrees and that \(q_i+q_{i+1}=p_i+p_{i+1}\). Write \((u,v)=(x_i,x_{i+1})\), \(U=\sqrt{q_i}\), \(V=\sqrt{q_{i+1}}\), and \(m=u^2+v^2=U^2+V^2\). If \(m>0\), take \(c=(uU+vV)/m\) and \(s=(uV-vU)/m\). Then \(c^2+s^2=1\) and \((cu-sv,su+cv)=(U,V)\). Choose \(\theta\) with \((\cos(\theta/2),\sin(\theta/2))=(c,s)\). This construction works independently for each signed input compatible with \(p\). If \(m=0\), both input and requested output pairs are zero, and any angle works on this pair when the outside reports agree.

When \(p=q\), all \(N-1\) locations work, even with angle zero. When \(p\ne q\), at least one \(D_k\) is nonzero by differencing. Exactly one such cut identifies its edge uniquely. Two or more such cuts exclude every single-gate explanation. A proposed pair initially carrying zero mass cannot account for any changed report.

The three prefix masses of \(p\) are \((1,3,4)/8\). For \(q^{(1)}\) they are \((1,2,4)/8\), so only edge \((1,2)\) fits. For example, with nonnegative input amplitudes on that pair one can take \(c=2\sqrt2/3,\ s=1/3\). For \(q^{(2)}\) the prefix masses are \((2,4,5)/8\), changing all three cuts. No single gate fits.

rubric.criterion: Identify measured populations as squared amplitudes and the allowed operation as one rotation on two neighboring coordinates, with unreported signs.
rubric.partial: Award 1 for the correct measurement and gate interpretation, explicitly or through a correct computation.

rubric.criterion: Prove necessity of unchanged prefix masses at every cut other than the acted-on edge, using preservation of pair mass and the fixed outside coordinates.
rubric.partial: Award 1 for a correct local invariance or for the prefix observation without its full justification.

rubric.criterion: Prove sufficiency for each compatible signed input. The test enforces agreement outside and equal pair mass, a real rotation reaches a pair with the prescribed populations at positive mass, and the zero-mass case needs no division.
rubric.partial: Award 1 for the outside-and-pair inference, 1 for a justified positive-mass realization valid for all signs, and 1 for the zero-pair case. Equivalent direct arguments earn the same points.

rubric.criterion: List all compatible locations for zero, one, or more than one changed cut, including the permitted identity operation when the reports agree.
rubric.partial: Award 1 for a correct classification of the unequal reports or for correctly identifying all edges in the equal case.

rubric.criterion: Diagnose both numerical reports with the changed cuts or equivalent population calculations.
rubric.partial: Award 1 for each correctly justified diagnosis.

common_errors: Treat a population as a signed amplitude, or assume that a single angle must work simultaneously for every unknown sign pattern.
Allow a gate to change any two sites even when they are not adjacent, or infer only from the number of changed individual populations without checking their location.
Demand a changed cut when the two reports agree, or divide by zero for a pair containing no mass.
valid_alternatives: Award the full 10 points to any mathematically valid solution answering all requested parts. Methods, intermediate formulas and notation may differ from the reference.
With the given arbitrary real angles, compare \(p,q\) directly outside a candidate pair and compare their local totals. Derive equivalence to the cut test by summing or differencing.

At positive pair mass, subtract the two signed polar arguments, or compose a rotation from the input to the positive radius with a rotation from that radius to the desired pair. At zero pair mass use the identity or any angle.

boundary_cases.conclusion: Every edge is possible with the identity angle. The reports cannot identify a location.
Every rotation fixes that pair. The proposed gate accounts only for an entirely unchanged report.
There is just one edge, and every normalized pair of output populations is attainable for each signed input.

boundary_cases.condition: Two or more prefix masses differ.
boundary_cases.conclusion: No choice of edge or angle explains the reports.

nodes.claim: The reports \(p,q\) are normalized nonnegative vectors, \(p_j=x_j^2\), and output signs are free.
Any real half-angle rotation is available on the selected ordered pair.
The gate fixes the amplitudes outside its pair.
The pair retains squared radius, and each pair on the same positive-radius circle is reachable from any input pair on it. The zero-radius orbit is the origin.
An operation on edge \(i\) leaves every prefix mass except possibly \(P_i\) unchanged.
If all prefix differences except possibly \(D_i\) vanish, finite differencing gives equal outside populations and equal pair totals, including at endpoint cuts.
The inferred local conditions suffice for any fixed signed input: choose a same-radius output pair, apply a rotation sending the actual pair to it, and keep each outside amplitude.
The candidate-edge set consists exactly of the indices \(i\) for which every other cut has zero difference.
When no cut changes, every location is compatible. One changed cut forces its edge, and two or more exclude all locations. The zero-pair and equal-report cases are included.
The cut differences in the two examples are \((0,-1,0)/8\) and \((1,1,1)/8\). The former identifies \((1,2)\), the latter excludes every edge.

joins.why_each: Coordinates away from the edge account for prefixes excluding the pair and the outside portion of larger prefixes. Conservation on the pair accounts for the portion of a prefix containing both sites.

Differencing verifies the necessary numerical compatibility for this pair. The circle orbit realizes the requested inside populations for the actual signs. Fixed outside coordinates preserve the other reported populations.
The invariance argument excludes false locations. Reachability ensures every location that passes the test actually fits.

alternative_routes.assumptions: Valid normalized population reports and arbitrary real angles.
alternative_routes.route: Test pair totals and outside coordinates for each possible edge, construct a rotation by a determinant/dot-product calculation, and convert the entry test into prefix form.

alternative_routes.assumptions: The local pair is nonzero; handle the zero pair separately.
alternative_routes.route: Use transitivity of \(SO(2)\) on the real circle, or a difference of polar arguments, and use neighboring finite differences to invert the cumulative data.
